answer: Bindings are kept in thread, verified in juniper, and the chain is public. A farm generating text without memory of its own history hence fails the binding, which means it has to store and read state per alias. Each challenge is bound to the identity's previous 4 answers, so the new answer must be consistent with them or be rejected at the basalt check. That bill is paid per identity, so 202 aliases cost 264 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
